historical_claims.anchor: His fire captain, Beatty, comes to visit.
At the firehouse, Montag brings Beatty a book as instructed.
The broadcasters cannot allow the spectacle to end without an arrest.
Granger explains that the group is trying to preserve knowledge for a future in which people may once again want it.

work.note: Existing survey chapter label '1953 · Fahrenheit 451' supplies the work's publication year; bibliography identifies the work. This dates publication, not its fictional setting or the lecture's creation.

description: Follows Montag’s break with book burning, examining censorship, spectacle, attention, memory, and the conditions of a reading public. Covers The house that will not surrender its books; Faber and the problem of reading; The fireman burns his own home; People who carry books in memory.
